Package io.github.jabrena.juno.api.io.net.email

package io.github.jabrena.juno.api.io.net.email
Basic SMTP send / POP3S read built on Wifi's connection: Smtp to send a plain-text message to one recipient, and Pop3Client to report the mailbox message count and read the newest message's From/Subject and a bounded plain-text body into caller-owned buffers.

Smtp upgrades a plaintext connection to TLS with STARTTLS on port 587 (the common mail-submission port), which the UNO R4 WiFi's native WiFiSSLClient cannot do — it only ever negotiates TLS from the first byte. This needs the third-party ESP_SSLClient library (arduino-cli lib install ESP_SSLClient), the same manual-install pattern as Mouse. Pop3Client instead uses implicit TLS on port 995 (POP3S), so it reuses WiFiSSLClient exactly like HttpsClient and needs no extra library.

Every host, username, password, and message field here must be a compile-time constant — a string literal, or a direct System.getenv("NAME") call with a literal name — for the same reason as io.github.jabrena.juno.api.io.net.http: Juno has no heap to build a runtime String from.

Scope, deliberately: one recipient, plain text only, no attachments, HTML, multipart MIME, folders, or OAuth2. ESP_SSLClient on this board validates the server host name but not its certificate chain (no CA bundle available to the software TLS stack), unlike HttpsClient/Pop3Client's use of the WiFi module's own firmware-backed validation — a deliberate tradeoff to fit STARTTLS in the UNO R4 WiFi's 32KB of RAM.
